If an image must lie in a lower-dimensional submanifold, assess the embedding into that submanifold; when a compact boundaryless manifold embeds into a connected manifold of the same dimension, invariance of domain and compactness force the image to be the whole target, so topology can rule out the claim.

edits.content: - For an equivalence, check both implications with definitions and hypotheses matched exactly; nearby notions or familiar formulations are not interchangeable without proving both directions. Answer the direction asked: an easy implication (such as isomorphism implying equal invariants) does not settle whether an invariant determines the object, and counterexamples outside the stated class do not refute a restricted claim. In reverse-mathematics questions, make the comparison over the stated base theory; familiar principles are not interchangeable unless both reductions hold there.
